question: Should I pay SDRs on demos booked or only on demos held + qualified?
answer:
**Pay on demos held + AE accepted (not booked).** An SDR booking a call that the AE cancels, or that doesn't qualify, doesn't create value. Paying on "booked" incentivizes calendar spam and SDR gaming (booking calls that won't convert). Paying on "held + qualified" requires SDR to set the right tone, prep the prospect, and show up. **The Booked vs. Held Problem:** **Scenario 1 (Booked): SDR gets $20 per demo booked** - SDR books 50 demos/month - AE holds 35 (30% no-show) - Of those 35, only 15 convert to SAL (43% qualified) - Effective "real demos" = 15 - SDR paid: 50 × $20 = $1,000/month - **Cost per real demo: $1,000 ÷ 15 = $66.67** - SDR learns: "Book volume, not quality." Spam tactics win. **Scenario 2 (Held + Accepted): SDR gets $15 per demo held, $25 AQL bonus** - SDR books 45 demos/month (fewer, better-qualified prospects) - AE holds 42 (93% show-rate; SDR prepared better) - Of those 42, 28 convert to AQL (67% qualified rate) - SDR base comp: 42 × $15 = $630 - SDR AQL bonus: 28 × $25 = $700 - **Total: $1,330/month; cost per AQL = $47.50** - SDR learns: "Prep matters. Show rate matters. Qualification matters." **Why Not Just "Booked"?** 1. **No-show rate inflation:** Companies paying on "booked" see 20–35% no-show rates (AE cancels, prospect no-shows, etc.). If SDR controls the booking tone and prep, no-show drops to 5–10%. You get 3x more actual customer conversations per SDR paycheck. 2. **AE toxicity:** AEs ignore SDR demos booked for "spam" reasons. They stop trusting SDR routing. Sales ops watches SDR → AE demo conversion drop from 80% to 40%. AE starts hiring their own SDRs instead of using the pool. 3. **Lead quality feedback loop:** If SDR gets paid for booking regardless, they never learn why certain lead sources convert and others don't. If SDR only gets paid for qualified demos, they ask AEs "Why did prospects X and Y not qualify?" and adjust their ICP hunting. **Best Practice: Held + Qualified (Multi-Tier)** **Tier 1: Demo Held (SDR Present or Prepped)** - $10–$15 per demo held by AE (SDR must have confirmation of attendance) - Cuts no-show gaming; incentivizes SDR to build rapport - If AE reports "no-show," SDR loses $10 (claw-back) **Tier 2: Demo Qualified (AE Accepted)** - $15–$25 per demo that AE marks "Qualified Lead" (budget + timeline + champion ID) - Incentivizes SDR to gather discovery info before handing off - Multi-touch SDR calls (3–4 calls before demo) reduce this friction **Tier 3: Pipeline Impact (Optional SPIFF)** - $50 bonus for each SQL that closes within 90 days - Rare at SDR level (requires CRM integration, 3-month lag) - More common at AE level (cash flow alignment) **Comp Structure Template ($50k OTE SDR):** | Activity | Payment | Monthly Target | Monthly Comp | |---|---|---|---| | Demo Held | $12/demo | 40 demos/mo | $480 | | AQL Accepted | $20/AQL | 28 AQL/mo | $560 | | AQL → Booked Demo | $10 bonus | 15 bookings/mo | $150 | | Total Variable | — | — | $1,190/month | | Base Salary | $40,500/yr | — | $3,375/month | | **Total Monthly** | — | — | **$4,565/month** | | **Annualized** | — | — | **$54,780** | **Why Not "Booked + Demo Held" (Both)?** Because then SDR gets paid twice for the same demo (once at booking, once at hold). You'd hit $2,000+/month comp on 40 demos, and you lose the quality incentive (SDR still spams to hit booking targets, then the held rate is what it is). **The No-Show Clawback:** If an SDR books a demo but the AE reports "no-show" or "not qualified," reclaim $10 (50% of hold payment). This incentivizes SDR to: 1. Call prospect 24hrs before to confirm 2. Brief prospect on what to expect 3.
